title: English Vocabulary 4 · Units 03–04
description: Advanced vocabulary for job advertisements, cover letters, interview preparation, recruitment decisions and employment offers, with precise register, collocations and word-pattern guidance.
sourceNotice: Prepared for personal study from the user-provided book. The choice of targets is grounded in the teaching units, their exercises and their answer key; all explanatory notes, Brazilian Portuguese translations and examples are newly written, without reproducing book passages or exercises.

audit.scope: Units 3 and 4 teaching and exercise pages, numbered glosses, recruitment examples, letter-writing guidance, employment offer examples, exercises 3.1–3.5 and 4.1–4.5, and answer-key entries.
audit.pronunciation: Broad British IPA is given only for short words where confident; expressions with no established entry-level transcription have blank IPA. IPA is not a connected-speech transcription.
audit.languagePolicy: Learner-facing descriptions, examples, titles, sections and notes are English only; Brazilian Portuguese appears only in pt fields.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared the original four PDF pages, their visual annotations and marginal notes, exercises and answer keys. Wrote new example sentences and usage notes. Independently checked collocations, British terminology, contrasts and Portuguese translations. Verified schema types, duplicate IDs and TTS-target speechText patterns programmatically. Live importer, browser TTS and speech recognition were not tested.
audit.limitations: No recorded MP3 is bundled. Browser import, synthesized pronunciation and speech-recognition compatibility need to be tested inside the VocabLab application. UK recruitment and employment terms may not map exactly to systems in other countries.

units.title: Unit 03 — Applying for a job
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 3. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Work and study · job advertisements and cover letters
learningObjectives: Interpret job advertisements, including career prospects, benefits, reporting relationships and salary expectations.
Write job applications using accurate cover-letter conventions, formal closings and relevant professional evidence.
Explain hands-on and customer-facing experience and describe teamwork and management responsibilities.
Use preposition patterns such as passion for, relevant to, support of and suitable for accurately.

sectionsChecked: A · A job ad, annotated vocabulary, role and salary terms
B · A cover letter, annotated vocabulary and application-writing guidance
Exercises 3.1–3.5 and Unit 3 answer key (PDF page 213)

items.example: The new coordinator needs excellent communication skills to manage a diverse team.
items.note: Usually plural; a common requirement in job advertisements.

items.example: Her genuine passion for customer service was clear in the interview.
items.note: Passion for is followed by a noun or an -ing form; genuine emphasises sincerity.

items.example: He accepted a challenging role that would broaden his technical expertise.
items.note: Challenging is often positive in recruitment language, suggesting rewarding difficulty.

items.pt: ambiente de trabalho dinâmico e de ritmo acelerado
items.example: She thrives in a fast-paced working environment where priorities change quickly.
items.note: Fast-paced means activities move rapidly; not necessarily chaotic.

items.example: The firm announced a new job opening in its research division.
items.note: An opening is an available position; openings is common in advertisements.

items.pt: responder hierarquicamente a; estar subordinado a
items.example: The firmware engineers report to the engineering director.
items.note: Report to identifies the person or position to whom an employee is accountable.

items.example: In this post, you will be responsible for testing embedded systems.
items.note: Use responsible for plus a noun or -ing, not responsible of.
items.speechText: be responsible for dealing with customer enquiries

items.pt: atender solicitações e dúvidas de clientes
items.example: The support team deals with customer enquiries throughout the day.
items.note: Enquiry is the standard British spelling; American English normally uses inquiry.

items.example: Previous experience with industrial networks is preferred but not essential.
items.note: Refers to experience gained before the current application or role.

items.example: Full training will be provided before the new recruits take calls.
items.note: Usually means that the employer provides the necessary preparation.

items.example: The post involves supervising laboratory operations.
items.note: Formal employment sense of post; not a social-media post.

items.example: The scheme offers promising career prospects for recent graduates.
items.note: Refers to future opportunities to progress in a career.

items.example: The assessment looks for leadership qualities rather than seniority alone.
items.note: Attributes that make someone capable of leading others.

items.example: The company is keen to develop talent through mentoring schemes.
items.note: Keen to plus infinitive expresses enthusiasm or willingness, common in British English.

items.example: The company offers a competitive salary and flexible working arrangements.
items.note: Implies pay comparable to or better than that of similar positions.

items.example: The benefits package includes dental cover and additional leave.
items.note: Benefits are extras offered alongside salary; may vary by country and company.

items.pt: plano de assistência médica; plano de saúde
items.example: Every permanent employee can join the healthcare plan.
items.note: A workplace benefit involving medical cover, not a medical treatment plan.

items.example: Employer contributions to the pension form part of the overall package.
items.note: Employment-related retirement provision; exact arrangements vary by country.

items.example: Staff can buy subsidised meals in the campus canteen.
items.note: Subsidised means partly paid for by another organisation; British spelling.

items.pt: candidatura on-line; inscrição eletrônica para uma vaga
items.example: Applicants must complete the online application before the deadline.
items.note: Refers to a job application submitted via a website.

items.example: Please attach your portfolio to the application form.
items.note: Form used to submit information when applying for a job or programme.

items.example: Recruiters may ask for salary expectations at an early stage.
items.note: Usually plural; states the pay an applicant hopes to receive.

items.example: Customer service is central to the company's retention strategy.
items.note: Refers to helping customers, not the company's commercial sales department.

items.example: Her promotion to team lead followed two years of excellent performance.
items.note: A move to a more senior position, not a sales discount in this context.

items.example: Your application will stand out if you explain your achievements clearly.
items.note: Stand out from the competition means attract attention for positive reasons.

items.example: A tailored cover letter can explain why you want the position.
items.note: Sent with a CV or résumé; covering letter is another British term.

items.example: Use the opening paragraph to highlight key points from your work history.
items.note: Highlight means draw attention to something important.

items.example: Update your CV before submitting an application.
items.note: Abbreviation of curriculum vitae; résumé is common in US job applications.

items.pt: Prezado(a) Senhor(a); saudação formal sem destinatário definido
items.example: Dear Sir or Madam is conventional when the reader's name is unknown.
items.note: Traditional formal greeting; addressing a named person is preferable where possible.

items.pt: segue em anexo; encaminho em anexo
items.example: Please find attached my CV and a brief research summary.
items.note: Formal email or letter formula; Attached is my CV is a shorter alternative.

items.pt: para apoiar minha candidatura; como parte da minha candidatura
items.example: I have included two references in support of my application.
items.note: Support of, not support to, in this fixed construction.

items.pt: candidatar-se a uma vaga; concorrer a um cargo
items.example: She plans to apply for a position in hardware verification.
items.note: Apply for a job or position; apply to an organisation.

items.example: The position requires experience with verification tools.
items.note: Often interchangeable with post or role in recruitment contexts.

items.example: His hands-on experience with FPGA prototypes impressed the panel.
items.note: Practical experience gained by actually performing tasks.

items.example: He decided to pursue a career in the field of robotics.
items.note: An area of professional activity or expertise, not a physical field.

items.pt: pertinente à função; relevante para o cargo
items.example: Focus on projects that are relevant to the role you are applying for.
items.note: Relevant takes the preposition to; not relevant with.

items.pt: com contato direto com clientes; voltado ao atendimento ao público
items.example: Her customer-facing role helped her develop negotiation skills.
items.note: Adjective describing work involving direct interaction with customers.

items.pt: pessoa que trabalha bem em equipe
items.example: He is a strong team player who shares credit for successful projects.
items.note: Common self-description in job applications; support it with an example.

items.example: The vacancy calls for managerial experience in a multidisciplinary team.
items.note: Experience of supervising people or management responsibilities.

items.example: The fellowship could help you develop your career in microelectronics.
items.note: Develop one's career describes longer-term professional progress.

items.word: look forward to hearing from you
items.pt: aguardo seu retorno; fico no aguardo de notícias
items.example: I look forward to hearing from you regarding the next stage.
items.note: Formal closing; look forward to takes -ing, not an infinitive.

items.example: She closed the letter with Yours faithfully because she did not know the recipient's name.
items.note: Traditional British formal ending after Dear Sir or Madam; varies internationally.

items.pt: executar um projeto; realizar um projeto
items.example: She carried out a research project on sensor reliability.
items.note: Carry out means perform or undertake work or an investigation.

items.example: The candidate highlighted three results from her previous role.
items.note: A verb meaning emphasise information in writing or speaking.

items.example: I am keen to gain experience in verification methodology.
items.note: Keen to followed by the infinitive expresses eagerness; especially natural in British English.

items.example: In my previous role as a systems engineer, I coordinated software releases.
items.note: Use in my previous role as + job title to introduce past responsibilities.

items.example: He led a team of engineers during the commissioning phase.
items.note: Past tense led, not lead; leadership means managing or directing a group.

items.pt: de meio período; em jornada parcial
items.example: She took a part-time position while completing her degree.
items.note: Commonly hyphenated before a noun.

items.example: He has a degree in electrical engineering.
items.note: Degree in identifies the field of study; avoid degree of for this meaning.

items.example: The advertised salary reflects the seniority of the position.
items.note: The regular pay for work; different from a benefits package.

items.example: Her prior experience makes her suitable for the supervisory position.
items.note: Suitable for is used of people, roles or purposes.

items.example: Several openings are expected in the company's graduate programme.
items.note: Plural form often used for vacancies in job advertising.

units.title: Unit 04 — Job interviews
units.source: Vocabulary study targets from published reference material; Unit 4. Page information, if available, is retained in sourceAudit.
units.category: Work and study · interview preparation, recruitment and job offers
learningObjectives: Prepare for interviews with a clear understanding of recruitment criteria, shortlisting and interview etiquette.
Use natural interview expressions for describing experience, professional development and responsibility.
Distinguish trainee and trainer, supervisor and superior, and in-house training from external provision.
Interpret job-offer language, including notice periods, paid leave, reporting structure and start date.

sectionsChecked: A · Preparing for interviews, annotated vocabulary and interview etiquette
B · During an interview, sample questions and key expressions
C · A job offer, employment documentation and annotated expressions
Exercises 4.1–4.5 and Unit 4 answer key (PDF pages 213–214)

items.example: The company is recruiting graduates for its verification department.
items.note: Recruiting refers to seeking and hiring staff, not merely assigning them tasks.

items.example: The hiring panel agreed on a set of criteria before reviewing CVs.
items.note: Criteria is plural; criterion is singular.

items.example: Each candidate must demonstrate relevant technical experience.
items.note: Applicant is anyone applying; candidate is often someone being considered for selection.

items.pt: ser selecionado para a lista de finalistas
items.example: She was shortlisted for an interview after the screening stage.
items.note: Means selected from a larger pool to proceed in the process.

items.pt: preparar-se pesquisando; fazer a pesquisa prévia
items.example: Before the interview, do your homework on the organisation's products.
items.note: Figurative idiom meaning research and prepare in advance.

items.pt: ensaio; simulação antes da situação real
items.example: We arranged a trial run of the interview with two colleagues.
items.note: A practice attempt that helps identify problems before the real event.

items.example: Practising difficult questions can boost your confidence.
items.note: Boost is a verb meaning increase or improve.

items.example: Two engineers will conduct the technical interview.
items.note: Conduct is a formal verb for organising and carrying out an interview.

items.example: The interview panel included a technical specialist and an HR manager.
items.note: A group of interviewers, not a single interviewer.

items.example: Discuss your training goals with your line manager.
items.note: British workplace term for the person directly managing your work.

items.pt: manter contato visual; olhar nos olhos
items.example: She made eye contact with each member of the panel while answering.
items.note: Contact is uncountable here; use make eye contact with someone.

items.example: Body language can communicate confidence even before you speak.
items.note: Non-verbal movements, posture and facial expressions.

items.example: A firm handshake can convey confidence where handshakes are customary.
items.note: Firm does not mean painfully forceful; etiquette varies by culture and setting.

items.pt: falar mais alto; falar de maneira mais audível
items.example: Could you speak up? The microphone is not working properly.
items.note: Often means increase volume; in other contexts it can mean voice an opinion.

items.example: The panel's first impression of a candidate can be shaped by the opening exchange.
items.note: Make a good first impression is the standard collocation.

items.example: The interviewer asked how she handles competing deadlines.
items.note: The interviewer asks questions; the interviewee answers them.

items.pt: explicar para nós passo a passo; detalhar
items.example: Could you talk us through the decisions behind your design?
items.note: Talk someone through something means explain its stages or reasoning clearly.
items.speechText: talk us through your professional experience

items.pt: profissional em treinamento; estagiário em formação
items.example: He joined the firm as a trainee accountant.
items.note: A trainee is learning a role; a trainer is the person providing training.

items.example: The company allocates a budget for professional development.
items.note: Includes training and growth in knowledge or skills.

items.pt: treinamento interno; capacitação realizada pela própria organização
items.example: All new employees receive in-house training on safety procedures.
items.note: In-house means provided within the organisation, unlike external courses.

items.example: New recruits attend a three-day induction programme.
items.note: Recruits are people who have recently joined an organisation.

items.example: She works well under pressure when deadlines are approaching.
items.note: Under pressure is the natural preposition pattern; not under stress in this use.

items.example: Your supervisor will review your progress every fortnight.
items.note: The person overseeing your work; not interchangeable with superior as a job title.

items.example: I would welcome the chance to take on more responsibility.
items.note: Take on means accept or start handling new duties; responsibility is often uncountable.

items.pt: preencher uma vaga; ocupar um cargo
items.example: The department hopes to fill the post by December.
items.note: Fill a post or vacancy means appoint someone to it.

items.example: Her contract specifies a one-month notice period.
items.note: Time between formally announcing departure and the end of employment.

items.example: Give specific evidence of your relevant experience during the interview.
items.note: Recruitment collocation; relevant to the job is the usual preposition pattern.

items.pt: contador em formação; profissional de contabilidade em treinamento
items.example: The trainee accountant assists with monthly reporting.
items.note: A person learning professional accounting work; not an accountant who trains others.

items.example: The project is developed in-house rather than outsourced.
items.note: Adjective or adverb for activities performed by an organisation's own staff.

items.example: The recruits met their supervisors on the first day.
items.note: Plural noun, contrasted with recruiting, the process of hiring.

items.pt: oferecer o cargo; fazer a proposta para a vaga
items.example: After the final interview, they offered her the position.
items.note: Offer someone the position is the usual construction.

items.word: an ideal fit for the role
items.pt: combinação perfeita para; perfeitamente adequado a
items.example: Her experience makes her an ideal fit for the research team.
items.note: Fit for describes suitability; also an ideal fit with a team or organisation.

items.example: The offer letter outlines the probation period and benefits.
items.note: Verb meaning summarise the main features rather than give every detail.

items.pt: licença remunerada; afastamento remunerado; férias remuneradas
items.example: Employees receive paid leave in accordance with their contracts.
items.note: Can cover paid holiday, family leave or other authorised time off; not necessarily annual leave alone.

items.example: The offer documents clarify the reporting structure for the team.
items.note: Explains who is accountable to whom within an organisation.

items.example: Please read the contract carefully and sign where indicated.
items.note: Standard instruction in employment documents and forms.

items.example: The employer asked for a response within five business days.
items.note: Normally excludes weekends and public holidays; exact holidays depend on location.

items.example: HR will complete the paperwork before your start date.
items.note: Uncountable noun for forms and administrative documents.

items.pt: data de início; data de admissão
items.example: Please confirm your preferred start date by Friday.
items.note: The agreed day employment begins; begin date is not the idiomatic term.

items.pt: oferta de emprego; proposta de contratação
items.example: She received a formal job offer after the second interview.
items.note: The employer's offer of employment, distinct from an invitation to interview.

items.example: The document sets out the salary and benefits attached to the role.
items.note: Terms of employment commonly specified in an offer.

items.pt: divulgar a vaga externamente; anunciar para candidatos de fora
items.example: If no internal candidate qualifies, the firm will advertise externally.
items.note: Contrasts with filling a post internally, using existing staff.

items.example: The trainer demonstrated the procedure to all new employees.
items.note: Someone delivering training, whereas a trainee receives it.

items.example: Taking on the senior role came with a salary increase.
items.note: Natural phrase for a rise in pay; distinct from a one-off bonus.
